newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine minister to meet Malan on Brazil imports.
newsitem.headline: Argentine minister to meet Malan on Brazil imports.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez will travel to Brazil next Tuesday for urgent discussions with Finance Minister Pedro Malan on Brazil's decision to slap restrictions on import financing.
Fernandez's travel plans were announced by his ministry's Institutional Relations Secretary Carlos Bercun.

Argentine Undersecretary for Foreign Trade Jorge Campbell warned Thursday that Brazil's move to limit the attractiveness of short-term financing for imports will have "grave consequences for exports."
Argentina is urging Brazil to exempt its regional trade partners in the Mercosur customs union -- Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay -- from the new restrictions on imports.

The Brazilian Central Bank, trying to head off a widening trade gap, ruled that most Brazilian importers with financing of less than 360 days will have to take out foreign exchange contracts on the day they retrieve their goods from customs.
Argentine exporters are protesting the "protectionist" new measures, which they say could harm the fledgling Mercosur's trading relationship with other markets.

"If Brazil doesn't find another way out, Mercosur's negotiating capacity on the international scene will be extremely weakened," the head of the Argentine Exporters' Chamber, Enrique Mantilla, told reporters.

"With these measures, we are going to look like a not very serious market and if there is no solution in the short term, the future of Mercosur could be in danger," said the head of the food exporters' lobby Copal, Alberto Alvarez Gaiani.

Argentina and Brazil are already engaged in trade disputes over fiscal subsidies Brazil grants to investments in its poor Northeast. Argentine President Carlos Menem is expected to try to unblock the disagreements on a visit to Brazil in late April.
